title: session.bind
description: Pair the hidden game's save slot with this Minecraft world. The server tells its client the world id (S→C); the client passes it to gen1-bridge (M→G). WORLD_SESSIONS_PLAN (WS2, WS3): M→G slot, save and continue carry the player's recorded or first-join choice; S→C regions carries the recorded choices.

incompatible.description: FOREIGN_POKEMON_PLAN §4.15, Q12: the region record's rules.compat.onIncompatible, what the link does with a member its game lacks; absent: visitor.

region.description: MG3 (several games): the region this message belongs to; absent = the legacy region. The client tags what it relays with its link's region; the server routes a tagged message to that region's link.

slot.description: WORLD_SESSIONS_PLAN §2.3 (WS2): M→G the slot recorded for this player and world (bound as it is, singleplayer or multiplayer; a slot the engine no longer has is refused session.no_slot); absent: none recorded yet.

save.description: WS2 (D3, D13, D14): M→G the player's first-join choice for this game: current (singleplayer: the engine's current slot), copy (multiplayer: the world's own slot written from a copy of the offline save), new (an empty slot of the world's own). Absent: today's rule (singleplayer the current slot, multiplayer the world's own slot).

continue.description: WS3 (D4): what gen1-bridge does once the slot is settled: play (CONTINUE, else NEW GAME, and the game is followed), park (CONTINUE and held where it loaded; a slot without a save stays at its title), title (nothing: the game stays at its title). Absent: title (today's behaviour).

regions.description: WS2 (§2.1): S→C the player's recorded choices for this world, per region (the legacy region by its id), so a server's client knows them as one opening its own world does.
